Completely underwhelmed
Jun 2023 • Friends
The restaurant is a beautiful space, we dined outside in a garden setting on the top floor of a lovely building with wonderful views of Hanoi. 

Service started well, the menu was big enough and interesting looking. Three of the four drinks we ordered came promptly, the fourth was left sitting on a service space nearby - Hanoi is warm in June and beer doesn’t stay cold for long. 

We ordered four separate main courses. Two of them arrived promptly, after a brief wait two of us started eating while our companions waited for their meals. We had to prompt the server, eventually the third of four mains arrived, the fourth didn’t come. 

By the time two of us had finished our meals we asked to cancel the fourth, the server came back and said it was too late to cancel but we could take it away in a doggy bag. 
The meal arrived anyway, the server we had been dealing with handed it off to a female colleague to try to bring it to us. We refused it and sent it back. 

The food we did eat was at best average. When the server realised we weren’t happy he avoided us, cutting us off from drinks. And by that I mean water, not alcohol. 

When the bill came we were pleased that they didn’t charge us for the unwanted dish, however there was a small amount for extras of peanuts that weren’t on our table. (Hand wipes and nuts are often served unasked for in Vietnam, if you don’t use them you don’t pay). 

Summary: uninteresting food, when I dine with friends we should all receive our meals at the same time - this was not a fast-food place, it was an evening out for us.

We recommend this restaurant
Dec 2022
We were very happy with the meal, with the service and with our talk with the general manager. The first room on the 8th floor that we were brought to was empty and had no seat cushions. We asked for another room and were brought to an ornate room on the 9th floor that had 5 out of 6 tables filled. The table and chairs (with cushions) looked very Chinese but were Vietnamese (and very heavy with very straight backs). The menu that we had found on facebook actually existed so we were able to order the dishes we had identified. We ordered a lime juice (VND 75,000) and water and were brought a bowl of pretty good peanuts and very good pickled celery. Our first dish was a crab and scallop soup (VND 165,000) which was good and had tasty pieces of crab and scallop in it. The next dish to arrive was the sticky rice (VND 75,000) which were a delightful surprise. Very light puffs of sticky rice that were also tasty. We were getting to like this restaurant. The salad with young coconut, shrimp and pork belly (VND 175,000) was very good and flavorful. The last dish to arrive was the hemibagrus fish (VND 295,000) made with galangal was delicious and served with an excellent sauce. That fish is a type of catfish and was tender and juicy. Our sever spoke good English and was very efficient. The general manager stopped by our table a couple of times and later sat with us. He told us we were in the VIP room and that one table had Vietnamese government people and another had tourists. He said his customers were about half Vietnamese. He recommended a restaurant to us that he thought we’d like and told us about his family. It was great fun. We had delightful evening and excellent food. We spent VND 1,271,600 US $52.93.

A Vietnamese restaurant that would not look out of place in Torquay!!!
Nov 2022
We were recommended this restaurant by a local tour guide. At first site, it looked OK as the decor was good. Once the service started, our main waiter - christened Manuel (as per Torquay reference) quickly showed that he was totally incompetent of taking an order for large group or answering questions on menu items. Even his manager was not much better. The wine waiter made an effort. Some starters arrived before order taking complete. Items that were not on the menu did in fact arrive. Some people's orders never arrived. Roughly 1/2 the group got what they wanted. When asked for cutlery, they replied it tastes better with chopsticks - which of course take time to learn. I had to send my chicken breast fillet back three times to attempt 1. removal of bones and 2 removal of dark meat. Eventually gave up. The wine was also a disaster - ending up paying USD82 for a mediocre Italian. When the meal was finished, we were offered waiver of 10%"Service" charge and fresh fruit on rooftop - we declined and said we would pay for actual food drink delivered and consumed and nothing more. I can guarantee you I will never be back.

One of its kind in Vietnam
Oct 2022
The restaurant not only boasts good food, it is also filled with historical artefacts worth millions of dollars. Spectacular and really eye-opening. Go to the roof top for a great view before you dine.

Spread over eight floors, the fare is mostly Vietnamese and these were deliciously excellent. Managed by a young man, the restaurant is a must-visit for all visitors to Hanoi. The service staff was very well-trained and attentive. 

The 17 of us had plenty of great food washed down with three bottles of whiskey and four bottles of wine. We were left overwhelmed by the food and ambience. It is a fantastic experience and all agreed that they would come back when they next visit Hanoi. 

What an evening, thank you Com Viet.

Exquisite Vietnamese
Apr 2022
This must be the most exquisite Vietnamese restaurant I've ever seen or visited. The entry takes your breath, the 9 different floors are so spectacular.

The food, I cannot express how magnificent the food is, elegant and sophisticated, lite, but with a punch. The Pineapple rice came in half pineapple, the colours, flovour and taste lit up our faces. The pigeon, rice paper wraps, beef in coconut all blew our minds.,

The kind staff and elegance of the service are of global quality, so much so that I have to say it is simply the best Asian restaurant I've ever been to.

Magnificent!!!

Quaint old style restaurant - suited to travellers
Mar 2017
Truc Bach is an area on the western edge of the Hanoi Old Quarter not far from West Lake. There are many hidden places here to eat and visit. 
One outstanding restaurant is Com Viet. Traditional Vietnamese decor and great service. Vietnamese food served in a pleasant environment with background music. 
A good selection of food, and a surprisingly good, if limited, wine list.
Certainly worth a visit if you are looking for traditional Vietnamese food and service, old style decor, very clean and comfortable at a reasonable price.
